title: Neural Collaborative Filtering
summary: Innovation: NCF replaces matrix factorisation's inner product with a neural network (GMF + MLP) that learns the user–item interaction function. Why it matters: the paper that pushed deep learning into collaborative filtering; its learned interaction view underlies modern embedding-based retrieval and ranking.

title: LightGCN: Simplifying and Powering Graph Convolution Network for Recommendation
summary: Innovation: LightGCN strips feature transformation and nonlinear activation from graph convolution, keeping only neighbourhood aggregation over the user–item graph. Why it matters: the standard strong baseline for graph-based recommendation and retrieval.

title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
summary: Innovation: SASRec uses a causal self-attention Transformer to model user behaviour sequences, balancing long-range context against recent-item signals. Why it matters: the reference sequence model that later industrial ranking stacks build on.

title: Wide & Deep Learning for Recommender Systems
summary: Innovation: jointly trains a wide linear model (memorisation of feature crosses) with a deep network (generalisation). Why it matters: the template for industrial ranking systems, deployed first in Google Play and copied across ads ranking stacks.

title: Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for Web-Scale Recommender Systems
summary: Innovation: PinSage runs graph convolutions on Pinterest's billion-scale pin graph with importance-based neighbourhood sampling and MapReduce inference. Why it matters: the first web-scale graph embedding system for retrieval, deployed in Pinterest candidate generation.

title: Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations
summary: Innovation: the two-stage deep candidate-generation + deep ranking design for YouTube, trained on watch history at billion-user scale. Why it matters: defined the retrieve-then-rank architecture that industrial recommendation (and ads) systems still follow. Note: RecSys '16 paper, not on arXiv — link goes to the DOI.

title: Neural Graph Collaborative Filtering
summary: Innovation: NGCF propagates embeddings over the user–item graph with interaction-aware messages, encoding high-order connectivity into the representations. Why it matters: established graph propagation as a core technique for collaborative retrieval.

title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
summary: Innovation: BERT4Rec trains bidirectional Transformers with a Cloze (masked-item) objective over user behaviour sequences. Why it matters: brought bidirectional sequence modelling to recommendation, influencing user-understanding models in ranking.

title: DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction
summary: Innovation: DeepFM shares embeddings between a factorisation machine and a deep network to learn low- and high-order feature interactions end to end. Why it matters: a standard CTR-prediction baseline for ads ranking.

title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
summary: Innovation: DIN's local activation unit weights each historical behaviour by its relevance to the candidate ad. Why it matters: founded attention-based user-interest modelling for CTR prediction in ads.

title: Deep & Cross Network for Ad Click Predictions
summary: Innovation: the cross network explicitly learns bounded-degree feature interactions alongside a deep network for ad click prediction. Why it matters: Google's feature-crossing design for ads ranking, and the predecessor of DCN-V2 used across web-scale ranking.

title: Deep Interest Evolution Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
summary: Innovation: DIEN adds an interest-evolution layer (AUGRU) that models how user interests drift over time. Why it matters: sequential interest evolution became a core ingredient of ads CTR models.

title: xDeepFM: Combining Explicit and Implicit Feature Interactions for Recommender Systems
summary: Innovation: xDeepFM's Compressed Interaction Network models vector-wise explicit high-order feature interactions, combined with a deep component. Why it matters: a standard explicit-interaction architecture for CTR prediction in ads ranking.

title: AutoInt: Automatic Feature Interaction Learning via Self-Attentive Neural Networks
summary: Innovation: AutoInt uses multi-head self-attention to learn explicit feature interactions in low-dimensional space for CTR prediction. Why it matters: showed attention-based interaction modelling as an alternative to FM-style crosses in ads models.

title: Ad Click Prediction: A View from the Trenches
summary: Innovation: FTRL-Proximal online learning with per-coordinate learning rates, plus Google's production lessons on feature hashing, calibration, and progressive validation for ad click prediction. Why it matters: the foundational large-scale online-learning recipe behind ads CTR systems. Note: KDD '13 paper, not on arXiv — link goes to the DOI.

title: Deep Learning Recommendation Model for Personalization and Recommendation Systems
summary: Innovation: DLRM systematised embedding tables plus MLP interaction for personalisation at Meta scale, with model parallelism for huge embeddings. Why it matters: the reference architecture and benchmark for large-scale recommendation and ads ranking hardware/software design.

title: DCN V2: Improved Deep & Cross Network and Practical Lessons for Web-scale Learning to Rank Systems
summary: Innovation: DCN-V2's improved cross network learns explicit feature crosses in a scalable, production-friendly form. Why it matters: widely deployed for web-scale learning-to-rank, including ads.

title: Product-based Neural Networks for User Response Prediction
summary: Innovation: PNN inserts a product layer capturing pairwise feature interactions (inner and outer products) before the MLP for user response prediction. Why it matters: an early explicit-interaction design for ads response prediction, still a common CTR baseline.

title: Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate
summary: Innovation: ESMM models CTR and post-click CVR jointly over the entire impression space, avoiding sample-selection bias and data sparsity in CVR estimation. Why it matters: the standard multi-task design for conversion prediction in ads ranking and bidding.

title: Multi-Interest Network with Dynamic Routing for Recommendation at Tmall
summary: Innovation: MIND uses capsule-style dynamic routing to extract multiple interest vectors per user for candidate generation at Tmall. Why it matters: multi-interest retrieval is now standard in industrial candidate generation.

title: Billion-scale Commodity Embedding for E-commerce Recommendation in Alibaba
summary: Innovation: EGES learns item embeddings from user behaviour sequences with side information (Graph Embedding with Side information) at billion-item scale for Taobao. Why it matters: industrial item-embedding retrieval used in Alibaba candidate generation.

title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval
summary: Innovation: TIGER generates semantic IDs autoregressively to retrieve items, replacing embedding-ANN retrieval with a generative model. Why it matters: started the generative retrieval line that industry recsys and ads systems are now adopting.

title: Behavior Sequence Transformer for E-commerce Recommendation in Alibaba
summary: Innovation: BST applies a Transformer block over user behaviour sequences inside Taobao's ranking model. Why it matters: early production evidence that Transformer sequence modelling lifts CTR in large-scale ranking.

title: Search-based User Interest Modeling with Lifelong Sequential Behavior Data for Click-Through Rate Prediction
summary: Innovation: SIM searches lifelong behaviour sequences (thousands of actions) with a two-stage search-then-attend design for CTR prediction. Why it matters: made lifelong user behaviour usable in production ads ranking.

title: Controllable Multi-Interest Framework for Recommendation
summary: Innovation: ComiRec extracts multiple interest vectors per user via dynamic routing or self-attention, with a controllable aggregation step for candidate matching. Why it matters: multi-interest retrieval deployed in Alibaba's matching stage, extending the MIND line.

title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
summary: Innovation: Meta's HSTU treats recommendation as generative sequence transduction over user action histories, scaling to trillion parameters. Why it matters: Meta's flagship generative recommendation model — the reference design for generative ranking/retrieval in production, including ads surfaces.

title: OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment
summary: Innovation: OneRec unifies retrieval and ranking in a single generative model with iterative preference alignment. Why it matters: an end-to-end generative alternative to the classic cascade, deployed at Kuaishou scale.

title: FiBiNET: Combining Feature Importance and Bilinear feature Interaction for Click-Through Rate Prediction
summary: Innovation: FiBiNET combines SENet-style feature-importance recalibration with bilinear feature interactions for CTR prediction. Why it matters: feature-importance plus interaction modelling used in Sina Weibo's ads CTR models.

title: Learning Tree-based Deep Model for Recommender Systems
summary: Innovation: TDM organises items in a maximum-heap tree and retrieves by beam search over tree levels, jointly learning the index structure and the model. Why it matters: tree-based retrieval became a standard candidate-generation approach at Alibaba scale.

title: Wukong: Towards a Scaling Law for Large-Scale Recommendation
summary: Innovation: Wukong's stacked factorisation machines show recommendation models follow scaling laws like LLMs. Why it matters: Meta's evidence that ranking quality keeps improving with model/data scale.

title: Applying Deep Learning To Airbnb Search
summary: Innovation: Airbnb's account of evolving search ranking from gradient-boosted trees to deep networks, including embedding-based personalisation and the production lessons learned. Why it matters: a candid industrial ranking case study — what actually moved bookings at Airbnb scale.

title: DHEN: A Deep and Hierarchical Ensemble Network for Large-Scale Click-Through Rate Prediction
summary: Innovation: DHEN ensembles diverse interaction modules hierarchically for large-scale CTR prediction at Meta. Why it matters: a production Meta ads-ranking architecture showing ensembling diverse interaction learners beats single architectures.
